Il carcinoma renale dà metastasi ossee l:
Renal carcinoma gives lytic bone metastases, often expansile, hypervascular and with a soft-tissue component that can be large. When the lesion involves the pedicle and posterior arch, the risk of instability (SINS) and of epidural extension increases: contrast-enhanced MRI is needed for cord compression and to plan treatment. Renal metastases are hypervascular: biopsy or surgery may bleed heavily, and they are often embolized before the operation.
